decision: Corrected eng review: G1 is two nutrient-name constants plus reconciliation, not a chemistry rule
rationale: Measured against the live FDC API after egress was opened. Gate passes 0/11 under current code. Cause is name drift (Glucose vs Glucose (dextrose), Total Sugars vs Sugars, Total NLEA), not galactose coverage. Reconciling the breakdown against Total Sugars supersedes the hardcoded safely-zero sugar list.

decision: Ship v0.5.0 (MINOR); keep package.json as the single version source, no VERSION file
rationale: USDA import went from never populating PAC/POD/Sugar to populating them for most ingredients -- new working capability, backward compatible. Declined the 4-digit VERSION file because package.json is already the project version of record and a second file is a second source of truth. Known consequence: gstack version tooling reports DRIFT_UNEXPECTED on this repo.

decision: Batch loop re-sequenced: Phase 0 prerequisites (serializer, canonical save, copy identity, print snapshot, test lane) block all feature work
rationale: Cross-model review found three capabilities the design assumed exist and do not. Save rebuilds the container as {Recipe, Ingredients} (recipe-manager.js:1195) and load copies only keys already on a fresh cRecipe (app.js:284), so any added field is silently dropped on round-trip. Print is a bare window.print() (recipe-manager.js:1400) that emits the live DOM including unsaved edits, so a QR could resolve to a formula never saved. copyFrom is Object.assign (core.js:108) so copy would clone a stable id. All verified independently. Also adds a batch record entity distinct from recipe, since a version can be churned repeatedly.

decision: P0.5: recipe containers are detached, deeply frozen snapshots built by one canonical path; library load extracted to its own module
rationale: buildRecipeContainer returned a view onto the live recipe while the cloud write is fire-and-forget: google-drive-storage.saveRecipe awaits findFileByName before updateFile stringifies, so edits made in that window entered the cloud copy while IndexedDB held the earlier state -- two backends disagreeing with no error and no attribution. Fixed by returning deepFreeze(structuredClone(container)) from one builder (snapshotForSave in recipe-manager.js), used by both library save and .ier export. Frozen as well as detached because detaching alone is a convention a later caller can break; module code is strict so a late write throws at the offending line. deepFreeze guards on isFrozen because structuredClone preserves cycles. structuredClone refuses functions and DOM nodes that JSON.stringify used to drop silently -- that refusal is reported via ErrorMsg rather than rethrown, since an uncaught throw in the async save handler is an unhandled rejection (the user clicks Save and nothing happens). Cloning drops prototypes, which matches what every reader already saw since both backends round-trip through JSON or a structured clone. Also closed review item 16: app.js onLoad moved to js/features/recipe-library-load.js as createLibraryRecipeLoader(deps) so the refusal-gate ORDER is testable; the .ier-import-vs-library-load backup divergence was reviewed and KEPT deliberately, since aligning it is a user-visible change and Phase 0 is structural only.

decision: P0.3 identity: in-container behind SchemaVersion 2 (RecipeId + SavedAt); index dropped; P0.6 guards merged into the cut; sync joins id-first with name fallback via pure extracted module
rationale: One Drive file is the only atomic unit (updateFile media-PATCH, google-drive-storage.js:431); a separate identity store forks ids on ordinary partial sync. Mint on save only (never load) prevents the migration fork. Outside voice caught: id-first join cannot see ids in listRecipes output so the join downloads bodies; save-as-new-name in the mainline flow duplicates ids unless copy-mints/overwrite-reprompt guards ship WITH the writer; the local index rebuilt blocker-2 resurrection inside the mitigation so it is deferred to P0.4; updatedAt is re-stamped at write time so SavedAt (author clock) travels in the v2 container. Pre-P0.2 strip threat closed operationally: reload every device at rollout, verify cache-busting. v2 with missing id loads-with-warning and re-mints on save; validation lives OUTSIDE containerProblem.

decision: Decision 6 AMENDED (T2.5, cross-model KEEP verdict): a save mints when keeping the id would put it on two local records; otherwise identity follows the recipe
rationale: Codex and Claude independently recommended KEEP for the confirmed different-id overwrite when nothing else carries the incoming id (the .ier import-collision case). Minting there protects nothing -- the target record's identity dies with its record either way -- while costing the surviving recipe its batch-history attachment and making the future id-first sync join manufacture duplicates instead of converging. The original letter was written about the rename-copy flow, where minting is genuinely required. Honest cost recorded: the id a save produces depends on a local scan, not predictable from the prompt alone.

decision: Decision 14: sync legacy conflicts REJECT outright — graft-with-warning withdrawn (maintainer, N=1 scope call)
rationale: For an app with one user, merge semantics for old-format-vs-identified collisions are not worth design time. An id-less body never replaces an identified record (SYNC_WARNINGS.LEGACY_CONFLICT in both planRecipeSync and decideRecipePush); handled on an exception basis via the warning. The identified-winner direction stays open so old records get carried forward, and scripts/migrate-legacy-recipes.js (throwaway) drains the legacy population. Accepted cost: a genuinely-newer legacy edit stalls until a human re-saves it. Remaining codex P2s banked, not designed around.

decision: P0.4 batch schema: a batch is a churn event, created AT PRINT in state planned; no-verdict is a value; ingredient order not meaningful so the diff is keyed by name; prose return path and defect taxonomy both CUT
rationale: Binder audit of 29 churned pages: 14 produced no result and silence is ambiguous, so outcome-time record creation reproduces the holes. Six of ten changes that altered the next batch came from prose, so the open field is where diagnoses live rather than a taxonomy.

decision: PR #11 merged as squash 644a598; branch restarted from main. Banked findings triaged by redesign disposition; the 11 REDESIGN-INDEPENDENT ones filed as issues #19-#24 grouped by root cause
rationale: The UI/UX replacement is about to become the focus, and a pending-todo file on a superseded branch is exactly how work gets orphaned. Grouping by root cause avoids the issue-per-step rot CLAUDE.md warns about.

decision: P0.4 schema needs revision before B1 starts — codex consult returned GATE FAIL with 13 P1s. Do not implement against the current text.
rationale: Four findings verified against the repo: the name-keyed diff collapses duplicate ingredient rows (design:455 already recorded this failure mode), the marks schema collapses flavor quality and intensity (audit:94 explicitly warns against it), SavedAt is absent though decision 22 syncs batches on it, and P0.4 never answers what happens to batches when a recipe is deleted (design:536).

decision: Decision 25: reprint is not a concept in this app. There is saving and printing; every print is a print event, two prints are two events. Batch mints on return, not at print.
rationale: Print-vs-reprint is beyond the app semantics (maintainer). This dissolves the decision 15/16 contradiction rather than patching it, and removes chain_root and the reprint-names-a-BatchId command from the print path.

decision: Decision 26: generalise the print log into a recipe event log (saved, printed, batch_recorded, deleted), stored on Drive as ONE IMMUTABLE RECORD PER EVENT, never an appended file.
rationale: Sync is LWW on whole records, so two devices appending to one log file silently lose events. Immutable per-event records make sync a union with nothing to resolve. Also clears the objection that killed the separate identity store: events are facts about the past, so partial sync means fewer facts, not wrong ones. A deleted event is a tombstone, closing issue #21.

decision: Decision 27: method is per-version and diffable, and decision 18 is FORMULA-SCOPED. Ingredient order is not meaningful; method order IS, and a reorder is a real change. Row and step ids survive versioning while RecipeId mints.
rationale: Sous vide temp drifted 75-77-80C across the binder and the record never states it. If decision 18 is not scoped, order-is-not-meaningful gets applied to method and reorderings vanish from the diff -- the same shape as the duplicate-ingredient own-goal.

decision: Decision 28: the printed sheet is the PRIMARY capture surface and the app screen is transcription. Design the paper form first; it drives the schema ergonomics.
rationale: Demonstrated, not argued: the olive-oil sheet pre-printed a draw-temperature prompt and it came back filled, against 2 of 29 in the binder. Prompts get answered. Corollary: only prompt for what is measurable at the bench -- cream butterfat came back blank and overrun came back as a question mark.

decision: OPEN QUESTION raised 2026-08-15: adopted external recipes are unmodeled. A third of the binder originates on recipe sites, is volumetric, and cannot be balanced. Either the app imports and converts (lossy) or external recipes become a reference-only record type carrying annotations and lineage but no PAC/POD.
rationale: Three web printouts (Serious Eats, Epicurious 1997, one from 2012) are annotated test runs sitting in the same binder as the Ice Ed sheets. 8 large egg yolks has no mass, only an estimate. This is upstream of the sheet format, since an adopted recipe still gets printed, made and annotated.

decision: Decision 29: the baker approach — metric weights for everything, including liquids. Grams is the only unit in the model; volumetric-to-weight conversion happens once at import, never at display. Supersedes the open question I raised about external recipes being unmodeled: import is planned and owns the conversion.
rationale: Maintainer call. The importer todo (2026-01-15-ai-recipe-importer-from-web.md) already owns volume-to-weight with an ingredient density database and confidence scores. Two things it should carry: countables like 8 large egg yolks need per-unit masses rather than densities, and the as-sourced measure should be retained so a row converted at a wrong density can be re-derived.

decision: P0.3 IS DEPLOYED — verified against the live site 2026-08-15. GitHub Pages serves the repo directly with no build step, so merging PR #11 to main was the deploy. Earlier STATE.md claiming NOT DEPLOYED was wrong.
rationale: Probed https://www.marklummus.com/icecream: recipe-serialization.js serves RECIPE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2, every P0.3/T4 file returns 200, and live recipe-manager.js is byte-identical to origin/main including the merge-boundary fixes. What remains are the two device-side rollout steps (hard reload, run the migration), not a deploy.

decision: The legacy migration moves INTO the app (Info & FAQ button) and scripts/migrate-legacy-recipes.js is deleted; rollout step 3 is now SYNC FIRST, then migrate
rationale: No browser on iPadOS has a console, so the one rollout step required on EVERY device was impossible on the maintainer primary device. Moving it in-app also bought review it never had: the script downgraded records from newer builds (unconditional SchemaVersion rewrite), restamped the SavedAt author clock sync orders by, listed with the lossy listRecipes (a partial listing drains what it got and reports success), and duplicated mintRecipeId (now in recipe-serialization.js). SYNC FIRST because the migration mints fresh ids, so a local legacy record whose synced copy is already identified would fork into a permanent DIVERGENT_IDENTITIES stall - a case that converges today; syncing first makes those copies arrive identified and the migration skips them.

decision: The app version is a bundle constant in js/features/build-info.js, never fetched from package.json; a unit test pins the two together
rationale: The panel answers what code am I actually running, which matters most when a stale cache means the answer is not what the server has. A fetched package.json would report the SERVER version while the browser ran older JS - confidently wrong in exactly the case you needed it. The constant ships inside the bundle, so it is stale precisely when the bundle is stale. VERSION had been hardcoded at 0.4.0 beta while package.json said 0.5.0.

decision: Decision 30: the printed formula is COPIED into the batch (SNAPSHOT_ROW + SNAPSHOT_INGREDIENT_DEF), never referenced; the printed event carries it between print and return
rationale: A reference dangles because the recipe keeps being saved. Embedding costs a few KB per churn against ~29 batches in two years; referential integrity cost is unbounded. Same trade P0.3 made for identity: one Drive file is the only atomic unit, so a batch that is one file cannot half-arrive. Corollary the amendment missed: mint-on-return makes the printed event the payload carrier, not a lightweight signal. Batch is authoritative, event log advisory.

decision: Decision 31: a batch is never deleted by its recipe. RecipeId on a batch is advisory and deletion does not cascade; the batch displays as an orphan carrying its own snapshot
rationale: A batch is a record of an evening that happened; the recipe is a plan. Deleting the plan cannot un-happen the evening, and decision 30 makes the batch fully readable without the recipe. Answers what batch-loop-design.md:536 said P0.4 owed and app.js:299 never defined. orphan_policy records which rule a batch was written under.

decision: Decision 32: overall_rating is unsigned quality on the batch and leaves the signed axis set
rationale: Decision 24s scale is bipolar because the binder vocabulary is bipolar. Overall has no bipolar reading: -2 and +2 would both mean bad, which breaks the one property that makes the scale legible. The one axis that is a ladder gets stored as a ladder.

decision: Decision 33: deltas are grouped — DELTA_GROUP 1-to-many DELTA, with a constraint_note and a to_pct_min/to_pct_max band
rationale: target/direction/from/to fails on two things actually written: increase fat to 8%, 9-11% optimal is a band not a point; Less Dextrose, more Sucrose is one coupled constraint holding PAC while lowering POD, and as two independent deltas the reason is lost. applied/applied_in_recipe_id is validated by try 7 and Try with 4 TBS rum on the external sheets.

decision: Decision 34: the formula diff keys on FORMULA_ROW.row_id, not the ingredient name; row ids survive versioning
rationale: batch-loop-design.md:455 already recorded that a name-keyed diff collapses duplicates, and the schema then did exactly that — Peppermint v1 has two Peppermint Candy rows. Also retires the rename-reads-as-remove-plus-add limit. General lesson: the own-goal was a decision applied one level wider than the evidence it was decided on, which is the same defect decision 27 caught in method.

decision: Decision 35: the diff RECOMPUTES both sides under one coefficient set; flagging drift is not enough
rationale: Flagging tells the reader the comparison is invalid without telling them what the valid one is — the dextrose case then reads as an unexplained warning next to numbers still wrong. Report drift first, then recompute under the newer set and label which was used, keeping as-printed values as provenance. Binder import inherits the rule.

decision: Decision 36: the typed prose field is primary, the photo is an attachment with transcribed full_text, and NOTHING is parsed — no OCR in scope
rationale: Decision 20s photograph-it-and-stop read as the photograph being the storage medium, implying OCR to get anything back and leaving the typed field ambiguous. Separates three things: OBSERVATION.prose typed and searched, PHOTO_ATTACHMENT.image for a human, full_text populated by transcription not extraction.
